content.description: What is the time complexity of accessing an element by index in an array?

questions.question: What is the time complexity of accessing an element by index in an array?
questions.explanation: Arrays use base address + offset, so element access is always constant time regardless of array size.

content.description: Which data structure follows the LIFO principle?

questions.question: Which data structure follows the LIFO principle?
questions.explanation: Last In, First Out — like a stack of plates. The last element pushed is the first to be popped.

content.description: What does the 'head' pointer in a singly linked list point to?

questions.question: What does the 'head' pointer in a singly linked list point to?
questions.explanation: Head always points to the first node of the list; it is null if the list is empty.

content.description: What is the best-case time complexity of Linear Search?

questions.question: What is the best-case time complexity of Linear Search?
questions.explanation: Best case: the target element is at index 0, requiring only one comparison.

content.description: Which of the following is NOT a linear data structure?

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a linear data structure?
questions.explanation: Trees are hierarchical (non-linear). Arrays, Stacks, and Queues are all linear data structures.

content.description: In a queue, insertion happens at ___ and deletion at ___.

questions.question: In a queue, insertion happens at ___ and deletion at ___.
questions.explanation: FIFO — enqueue (insert) at the rear, dequeue (delete) from the front.

content.description: What is the average-case time complexity of Binary Search?

questions.question: What is the average-case time complexity of Binary Search?
questions.explanation: Binary Search halves the search space at each step. The array must be sorted beforehand.

title: Stable Sorting with O(n log n) Worst Case

content.description: Which sorting algorithm is stable AND has O(n log n) worst-case time complexity?

questions.question: Which sorting algorithm is stable AND has O(n log n) worst-case time complexity?
questions.explanation: Merge Sort is always O(n log n) in all cases and is stable — it preserves the relative order of equal elements.

content.description: How much space does recursive DFS on a graph with V vertices use?

questions.question: How much space does recursive DFS on a graph with V vertices use?
questions.explanation: The recursive call stack depth is at most V in the worst case (a linear chain graph).

content.description: What is the height of a complete binary tree with n nodes?

questions.question: What is the height of a complete binary tree with n nodes?
questions.explanation: Height = ⌊log₂(n)⌋ — it grows logarithmically as each level roughly doubles the node count.

content.description: In which traversal of a BST are nodes visited in ascending sorted order?

questions.question: In which traversal of a BST are nodes visited in ascending sorted order?
questions.explanation: In-order traversal (Left → Root → Right) on a BST always produces elements in sorted ascending order.

content.description: What is the worst-case time complexity of inserting into a Hash Table with chaining?

questions.question: What is the worst-case time complexity of inserting into a Hash Table with chaining?
questions.explanation: Worst case: all n keys hash to the same bucket, forming a chain of length n — degrading to linear search.

content.description: Which algorithm finds the shortest path in an unweighted graph?

questions.question: Which algorithm finds the shortest path in an unweighted graph?
questions.explanation: BFS explores the graph level by level, guaranteeing the shortest path by edge count in unweighted graphs.

content.description: What is the time complexity of building a Max-Heap from an unsorted array?

questions.question: What is the time complexity of building a Max-Heap from an unsorted array?
questions.explanation: Floyd's bottom-up heapify is O(n) — most nodes are near the leaves and require only O(1) work each.

content.description: Which problem CANNOT be solved using Dynamic Programming?

questions.question: Which problem CANNOT be solved using Dynamic Programming?
questions.explanation: Hamiltonian Path is NP-complete — no known polynomial-time DP solution exists for the general case.
